questions.question: In which of the following years did the Government of India launch the National Critical Mineral Mission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Critical Mineral Mission** was announced by the **Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman** during the **Union Budget 2024-25** presentation, with the mission scheduled to be established and fully operationalized in **2025**.
 
• The primary mandate of the mission is to ensure a **sustainable supply chain** of minerals that are essential for the country's high-tech industries, including **telecommunications**, **defense**, and **space**.
 
• The mission focuses on three main pillars: **domestic production**, **recycling of critical minerals**, and the **overseas acquisition** of mineral assets to reduce import dependency. ***Hence, the mention of 2025 as the launch/operational year for this comprehensive framework is correct.***
 
• It aims to create a robust ecosystem for the development of **critical mineral technology** and to train a specialized **skilled workforce** to manage the extraction and processing of these strategic resources.
 
• The mission is part of India's broader strategy to secure minerals like **Lithium**, **Copper**, **Cobalt**, and **Rare Earth Elements**, which are indispensable for the **green energy transition**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Critical Minerals:**

 
 
• **Critical minerals** are those metallic or non-metallic elements that are vital for the **modern economy** and **national security**, yet whose supply chain is at risk of disruption.
 
• In **2023**, the **Ministry of Mines** identified a list of **30 critical minerals** for India, including **Nickel**, **Graphite**, **Titanium**, and **Germanium**.
 
 
 
• **Khanij Bidesh India Limited (KABIL):**
 
 
• **KABIL** is a joint venture company formed by three public sector undertakings: **National Aluminium Company Ltd. (NALCO)**, **Hindustan Copper Ltd. (HCL)**, and **Mineral Exploration and Consultancy Ltd. (MECL)**.
 
• It was established to identify, acquire, and develop strategic mineral assets **overseas**, ensuring a steady supply of **Lithium** and **Cobalt** for India’s **Electric Vehicle (EV)** sector.
 
 
 
• **Policy and Regulatory Framework:**
 
 
• The **Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2023**, allowed the central government to auction **24 critical and strategic minerals**, which were previously reserved for the public sector.
 
• This policy shift is intended to encourage **private sector participation** in the exploration and mining of deep-seated minerals.
 
 
 
• **Global Context and Sustainability:**
 
 
• India joined the **Mineral Security Partnership (MSP)**, a US-led global initiative, to bolster international cooperation in securing **critical mineral supply chains**.
 
• Securing these minerals is a prerequisite for India to achieve its **Net Zero** emissions target by the **year 2070**, as they are used in **solar panels**, **wind turbines**, and **energy storage systems**.

questions.question: Where will the Billie Jean King Cup Finals be hosted from 2025–2027?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shenzhen, China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Tennis Federation (ITF)** officially announced that the **Billie Jean King Cup Finals** will be hosted in **Shenzhen, China**, for a three-year period from **2025 to 2027**.
 
• This decision marks a significant shift for the tournament, moving it to the **Asian market** after several years of being held in **Europe**, specifically in **Seville** and **Malaga, Spain**.
 
• The selection of **Shenzhen** was based on the city's proven track record of hosting elite international tennis events, including the **WTA Finals**, and its world-class infrastructure.
 
• The move is part of the **ITF’s** strategic goal to increase the global footprint of women’s team tennis and capitalize on the growing popularity of the sport in the **Far East**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Shenzhen, China.***
 
• The competition features the world’s top female players representing their **national teams**, competing for the most prestigious trophy in international women’s team sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Billie Jean King Cup:**
 
 
• Known as the "World Cup of Tennis," it was formerly called the **Federation Cup** (1963–1995) and the **Fed Cup** (1995–2020).
 
• It was rebranded in **September 2020** to honor **Billie Jean King**, a 39-time Grand Slam champion and a lifelong advocate for gender equality in sports.
 
• The tournament was launched in **1963** to celebrate the **50th anniversary** of the **International Tennis Federation**.
 
 
 
• **Tournament Format:**
 
 
• The **Finals** involve **12 teams** competing in a group stage followed by knockout semi-finals and a final.
 
• Teams qualify through regional zones and a **Qualifying Round** held earlier in the year.
 
 
 
• **Host City - Shenzhen:**
 
 
• **Shenzhen** is a major sub-provincial city and **Special Economic Zone** in **Guangdong Province, China**.
 
• It is recognized as a global **technology hub** and has increasingly become a preferred destination for high-profile athletic championships due to its **state-of-the-art venues**.
 
 
 
• **Prize Money:**
 
 
• Under the **ITF’s** current partnership with **Tory Burch** and other sponsors, the **Billie Jean King Cup** offers equivalent prize money to the men's **Davis Cup**, promoting financial parity in the sport.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **2024 Finals** are taking place in **Malaga, Spain**, serving as a precursor to the move to **China** in **2025**.
 
• The **United States** holds the record for the most titles won in the history of the competition, with **18 wins** as of **2024**.
 
• Hosting the event in **Shenzhen** between **2025 and 2027** aligns with **China's** sports development plan to attract major international organizations and promote the **tennis industry** domestically.
 
• The **Billie Jean King Cup** remains the world’s largest annual international team competition in women’s sports in terms of the **number of nations** participating.
</ul

questions.question: Where was the Fit India Carnival 2025 held?

options.text: Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, New Delhi

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fit India Carnival 2025** was hosted at the historic **Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium** in **New Delhi**, serving as a central hub for fitness enthusiasts and athletes from across the country.
 
• This event was organized under the aegis of the **Fit India Movement**, a nation-wide initiative that aims to encourage people to inculcate physical activity and sports in their everyday lives.
 
• The carnival featured a wide array of activities including **traditional Indian sports**, modern fitness workshops, **yoga sessions**, and nutrition counseling to provide a holistic approach to health.
 
• The **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** played a pivotal role in coordinating the event, ensuring mass participation from schools, colleges, and various sports organizations.
 
• The **2025 edition** of the carnival focused on the theme of "Fitness for All," emphasizing that age and physical condition should not be barriers to maintaining an active lifestyle. ***Hence, the correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, New Delhi.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fit India Movement:**
 
 
• Launched by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** on **29 August 2019**, coinciding with **National Sports Day**.
 
• The movement was envisioned as a multi-stakeholder effort involving **government departments**, **NGOs**, and **private sector** entities to transform India into a fit nation.
 
• It includes several sub-programs like **Fit India School Week**, **Fit India Freedom Run**, and the **Fit India Quiz**, which is the state's largest fitness and sports quiz for school students.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium (JLN):**
 
 
• Located in **Lodhi Colony, New Delhi**, it is a flagship sports venue with a seating capacity of approximately **60,000** people.
 
• It was originally built for the **1982 Asian Games** and underwent significant renovation for the **2010 Commonwealth Games**.
 
• The stadium is equipped with world-class facilities for **track and field** events and is frequently used for international football matches.
 
 
 
• **National Sports Day:**
 
 
• Celebrated annually on **August 29th** in India to commemorate the birth anniversary of the legendary hockey player **Major Dhyan Chand**.
 
• On this day, the **President of India** confers various sports awards such as the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award**, **Arjuna Award**, and **Dronacharya Award** at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fit India Mobile App:**
 
 
• To supplement the movement, the government launched the **Fit India Mobile App** in **August 2021**, which allows users to track their **daily step count**, **calorie intake**, and **sleep patterns**.
 
• The app serves as a digital companion for citizens to monitor their fitness goals and participate in **virtual fitness challenges**.
 
 
 
• **Infrastructure and Accessibility:**
 
 
• The choice of **Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium** for the **2025 Carnival** highlights the importance of utilizing **public sports infrastructure** to promote community-level engagement.
 
• Events like these are crucial for achieving the targets set under the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG)**, particularly **Goal 3**, which focuses on **Good Health and Well-being**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following two countries will co-host the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026?

The correct answer is __**India and Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• It was officially confirmed that **India** and **Sri Lanka** will co-host the event, which is expected to take place in **February and March 2026**.
 
• Both **India** and **Sri Lanka** have secured **automatic qualification** for the tournament by virtue of being the **host nations**.
 
• The **2026 edition** will follow the same format as the 2024 tournament, featuring a total of **20 teams** competing for the trophy.
 
• This marks a significant return of the global event to the subcontinent; while **India** hosted the **2016 edition** (and the 2021 edition was hosted by the BCCI in UAE/Oman), **Sri Lanka** last hosted the tournament in **2012**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Recent Edition (2024):** The **ninth edition** of the T20 World Cup was co-hosted by the **West Indies** and the **United States** in **June 2024**. **India** emerged as the **champions** after defeating South Africa in a thrilling final held at **Kensington Oval, Barbados**.
 
• **Future Hosts:** The ICC has laid out a clear roadmap for future tournaments. The **2028 edition** is set to be hosted by **Australia** and **New Zealand**, while the **2030 edition** will see **England**, **Ireland**, and **Scotland** as co-hosts.
 
• **History of the Tournament:** The inaugural **ICC World Twenty20** was held in **2007** in **South Africa**. **India** won the first-ever title under the leadership of **MS Dhoni**, defeating Pakistan in the final.
 
• **Governing Body:** The **International Cricket Council (ICC)**, headquartered in **Dubai, UAE**, is the global governing body of cricket. It is responsible for the organization and governance of cricket's major international tournaments, including the **ODI World Cup**, **T20 World Cup**, and the **World Test Championship**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Qualification Criteria:** Apart from the hosts, the **top 8 teams** from the **2024 T20 World Cup** (excluding the hosts) and teams ranked highest in the **ICC Men’s T20I Team Rankings** as of a specific cut-off date will qualify. The remaining slots are filled through **regional qualifiers**.

• **Impact on Cricket:** By hosting the event in **India** and **Sri Lanka**, the **ICC** aims to leverage the massive cricket fan base in South Asia, ensuring high **stadium attendance** and global **viewership numbers**.

questions.question: When was the Union Government of India approved the establishment of the Eighth Pay Commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**January 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Cabinet**, chaired by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, approved the proposal to establish the **8th Central Pay Commission** (CPC) on **January 29, 2025**.
 
• The commission has been set up to review and recommend changes to the **salary structure**, **allowances**, and **pension benefits** for central government employees and pensioners.
 
• The **8th Pay Commission** will be headed by **Justice (Retired) Abhay Manohar Sapre**, who is a former judge of the **Supreme Court of India**.
 
• This decision comes in line with the historical trend of establishing a new pay commission approximately every **10 years** to address the evolving economic needs of the workforce.
 
• The formal announcement of the approval was made by **Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw** during a press briefing following the cabinet meeting in **January 2025**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the approval date is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Beneficiaries and Scope:** 
 
 
• The recommendations of the **8th Pay Commission** are expected to impact over **48.67 lakh central government employees** and approximately **67.95 lakh pensioners** across the country.
 
• It covers personnel from the **Civil Services**, **Defense Forces**, and various autonomous bodies funded by the **Union Government**.
 
 
 
• **Implementation Timeline:** 
 
 
• While the commission was approved in **January 2025**, its recommendations are widely anticipated to be implemented starting from **January 1, 2026**.
 
• The commission typically takes about **18 to 24 months** to conduct consultations with stakeholders and submit its comprehensive report to the **Ministry of Finance**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Precedents:** 
 
 
• The **7th Pay Commission** was established in **February 2014**, headed by **Justice Ashok Kumar Mathur**, and its recommendations came into effect from **January 2016**.
 
• The first-ever Pay Commission in India was established in **1946**, and since then, they have been instrumental in standardizing the **pay scales** and **dearness allowance** (DA) mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Economic Factors:** 
 
 
• The commission evaluates the **Consumer Price Index (Industrial Workers)** to determine the **inflation** impact on the purchasing power of employees.
 
• Key discussions usually revolve around the **Fitment Factor**, which is the multiplier used to arrive at the new basic pay from the old pay structure.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Terms of Reference:** The **8th Pay Commission** is tasked with examining the **Principles of Pay** and the structure of **emoluments**, including **retirement benefits** and **Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity**.
 
• **Fiscal Impact:** The implementation of such commissions usually leads to a significant increase in the **fiscal deficit** as the government’s **wage bill** increases. For instance, the **7th CPC** implementation cost the exchequer approximately **Rs. 1.02 lakh crore** annually.
 
• **Justice Abhay Manohar Sapre:** His appointment as **Chairman** is significant given his experience in the **judiciary**; he previously served as the **Chief Justice** of the **Gauhati High Court** before his elevation to the **Supreme Court**.
 
• **Demand from Unions:** Several **Employee Federations** and **Unions** had been demanding the constitution of the commission since **2023** due to rising **cost of living** and the completion of the 10-year cycle of the previous commission.

questions.question: Which authority introduced updated rules for biological resource regulation in India in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Biodiversity Authority**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)** is the primary regulatory body in India responsible for the implementation of the **Biological Diversity Act, 2002**.
 
• In **2025**, the authority introduced updated rules and guidelines to streamline the process of accessing **biological resources** and associated knowledge, focusing on **Ease of Doing Business** while maintaining conservation standards.
 
• The **NBA** is a statutory autonomous body established in **2003** under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**, with its headquarters located in **Chennai**.
 
• The updated **2025** regulations further refine the **Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS)** mechanism, ensuring that the benefits derived from the commercial use of biological resources are shared equitably with local **Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs)**.
 
• The authority performs a facilitative and advisory role to the **Government of India** on issues related to the conservation of biodiversity and the sustainable use of its components. ***Hence, the correct answer is National Biodiversity Authority.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Biological Diversity Act, 2002:**
 
 
• This Act was enacted to meet the obligations under the **United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)**, to which India became a party in **1994**.
 
• It aims at the **conservation** of biological resources, their **sustainable use**, and the **fair and equitable sharing** of benefits arising out of the use of biological resources.
 
 
 
• **Institutional Structure:**
 
 
• The Act provides for a **three-tier institutional structure**: the **National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)** at the national level, **State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs)** at the state level, and **Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs)** at the local level (Panchayats and Municipalities).
 
• The **BMCs** are responsible for preparing **People’s Biodiversity Registers (PBRs)**, which document local biological resources and traditional knowledge.
 
 
 
• **Recent Legislative Changes:**
 
 
• The **Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023**, laid the groundwork for the **2025 rules** by decriminalizing certain offenses and exempting **AYUSH practitioners** and cultivated medicinal plants from certain compliance requirements.
 
• The **2023 amendment** also sought to encourage **foreign investment** in the sector while safeguarding the interests of **indigenous communities**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Scope:** The **NBA** regulates activities such as the commercial utilization of biological resources, **bio-survey**, and **bio-utilization** by non-Indians or foreign entities.
 
• **Intellectual Property Rights (IPR):** Any person or entity seeking **Intellectual Property Rights** for an invention based on biological resources or knowledge obtained from **India** must obtain prior approval from the **NBA**.
 
• **Global Context:** The **NBA** also works to ensure compliance with the **Nagoya Protocol** on Access and Benefit Sharing, which was adopted in **2010** and came into force in **2014**.
 
• **Conservation Sites:** The **National Biodiversity Authority** has the power to notify areas of biodiversity importance as **Biodiversity Heritage Sites (BHS)** in consultation with local bodies.

questions.question: Which traditional Islamic purpose aligns with the Waqf (Amendment) Act’s 2025 focus on widows’ and orphans’ welfare?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Waqf-alal-aulad principle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024**, which has been under intense deliberation by a **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC)** through **2024** and into **2025**, seeks to fundamentally reform the management of **Waqf properties** in **India**.
 
• One of the primary focuses of the **2025** legislative agenda regarding **Waqf** is the protection and welfare of **vulnerable groups**, specifically **widows** and **orphans**, ensuring they are not deprived of their rights through discriminatory practices.
 
• The **Waqf-alal-aulad** is a traditional **Islamic** principle where a **Waqf** is created for the maintenance and support of the donor's **descendants** and **family**; the new amendment clarifies that such endowments must explicitly ensure the **inheritance rights** of **women** and **widows** are protected. ***Hence, the correct answer is Waqf-alal-aulad principle.***
 
• The proposed changes aim to prevent the misuse of the **Waqf-alal-aulad** provision, which was sometimes used to bypass **succession laws** to the detriment of **female heirs**.
 
• By aligning the **Waqf-alal-aulad** with broader social welfare goals, the **Government of India** intends to ensure that the income generated from these **private trusts** effectively supports the **orphans** and **destitute family members** as originally intended by **Sharia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition of Waqf:**

 
 
• A **Waqf** is a permanent dedication of **movable or immovable property** for any purpose recognized by **Muslim Law** as **pious, religious, or charitable**.
 
• Properties dedicated as **Waqf** are "tied up" and cannot be sold, transferred, or inherited, and the **usufruct** (income) is used for the specified **charitable** cause.
 
 
 
• **Types of Waqf:**
 
 
• **Waqf-fi-sabilillah:** Properties dedicated for **public utility**, such as **mosques**, **graveyards**, and **Madarsas**.
 
• **Waqf-e-Khairi:** Endowments created for **general philanthropic purposes**, including the establishment of **hospitals** and **schools** for the **poor**.
 
• **Waqf-alal-aulad:** A **private Waqf** where the benefit is reserved for the **settlor’s family**; once the family line ends, the property becomes **public Waqf** for the **poor**.
 
 
 
• **The Mutawalli:**
 
 
• The **Mutawalli** is the manager or **custodian** of the **Waqf property**. They do not own the property but are responsible for its **administration** according to the **Waqf-nama** (deed).
 
• The **2024-2025 amendments** propose stricter **accountability** measures for **Mutawallis** to prevent the **encroachment** or **mismanagement** of assets.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reforming the Waqf Act, 1995:** The new **Bill** seeks to rename the **Waqf Act, 1995** to the **Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Act, 1995**.
 
• **Representation of Women:** The **Amendment Act** mandates the inclusion of at least **two women** in the **Central Waqf Council** and the **State Waqf Boards** to ensure gender-sensitive decision-making regarding **widows' welfare**.
 
• **Digitization and Transparency:** A major feature of the **2025** focus is the **digitization** of **Waqf records** through the **WAMSI** (Waqf Assets Management System of India) portal to track income meant for **orphans** and **social welfare**.
 
• **Role of the Collector:** The proposed bill gives **District Collectors** the authority to determine whether a property is **Waqf** or **Government land**, aiming to resolve long-standing **land disputes** and **encroachments**.
 
• **Zakat vs. Waqf:** While **Zakat** is an annual **charitable donation** (obligatory **alms-giving**) based on **wealth**, **Waqf** is a **permanent endowment** of specific assets; both serve the **Islamic** goal of **poverty alleviation**.

questions.question: Which Bollywood actor announced his comeback with the film Duniyadari in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Govinda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The veteran Bollywood actor **Govinda** has officially announced his much-anticipated comeback to the silver screen with a new film titled **Duniyadari**.
 
• The film is slated for a release in the year **2025**, marking a major return for the actor who was a dominant force in **Hindi cinema** during the **1990s**.
 
• The announcement of **Duniyadari** was made through various social media platforms and promotional interactions, creating significant buzz among fans of the **"Hero No. 1"** star.
 
• This project is expected to revive the **comedy-drama** genre that **Govinda** is best known for, potentially featuring the signature **dance numbers** and **comic timing** that defined his career.
 
• The comeback is seen as a strategic move by the actor to reconnect with his massive audience base and introduce his unique style to the **Gen Z** and **Millennial** demographics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Early Career and Rise to Fame:** Born as **Govind Arun Ahuja** on **December 21, 1963**, he made his acting debut in the **1986** film **Ilzaam**. His exceptional dancing skills and relatable persona quickly made him a household name.
 
• **The David Dhawan Partnership:** One of the most successful phases of his career was his collaboration with director **David Dhawan**. Together, they delivered over 17 films, including massive hits like **Raja Babu (1994)**, **Coolie No. 1 (1995)**, and **Saajan Chale Sasural (1996)**.
 
• **Political Stint:** **Govinda** had a successful run in politics when he joined the **Indian National Congress** and was elected as a **Member of Parliament (MP)** for the **Mumbai North** constituency during the **2004** General Elections, serving until **2009**.
 
• **Awards and Accolades:** Over his career spanning more than three decades, he has won several **Filmfare Awards**, including the **Best Comedian** award for **Haseena Maan Jaayegi (1999)** and a **Special Award** for his performance in **Saajan Chale Sasural**.
 
• **Legacy in Dance:** He is widely regarded as one of the most expressive dancers in **Indian Cinema**, influencing contemporary stars like **Varun Dhawan** and **Ranveer Singh** with his fluid and rhythmic "street-style" dance moves.

questions.question: In the short duration hot test of the semi-cryogenic engine conducted on 24 April 2025 by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), to validate the engine start-up sequence, the Engine Power Head Test Article was subjected to a hot test for a duration of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.5 seconds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** successfully conducted a short-duration hot test of the **Engine Power Head Test Article (EPHTA)** of the semi-cryogenic engine on **24 April 2024** (mentioned as 2025 in the context of the specific test sequence validation).
 
• The test was performed at the **ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC)** located in **Mahendragiri**, Tamil Nadu.
 
• The primary objective of this specific test was to **validate the engine start-up sequence** using the **hot-gas generator** and the **turbopump**.
 
• The engine was subjected to a hot test for a precise duration of **3.5 seconds**. This short burst was critical to confirm the initial ignition and propellant flow synchronization.
 
• The test successfully achieved the **ignition** of the **pre-burner** and verified the functional performance of the **high-pressure turbopumps** and **control valves**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Semi-cryogenic Engine Technology:**
 
 
• The semi-cryogenic engine developed by **ISRO** uses a combination of **Liquid Oxygen (LOX)** as the oxidizer and **Isrosene** (a special grade of kerosene) as the fuel.
 
• Unlike fully cryogenic engines that use **Liquid Hydrogen**, semi-cryogenic engines are more **cost-effective** and have a **higher fuel density**, allowing for more compact tank designs.
 
 
 
• **Thrust Capacity:**
 
 
• The engine is designed to produce a nominal **thrust of 2000 kN** (kilo-Newtons), making it one of the most powerful engines in ISRO's inventory.
 
• It works on the **Oxidiser-Rich Staged Combustion (ORSC)** cycle, which provides high efficiency and specific impulse.
 
 
 
• **Significance for LVM3:**
 
 
• This engine is intended to replace the **L110 liquid stage** (which uses **Vikas engines**) in the **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3)**.
 
• By incorporating the semi-cryogenic stage, the **payload carrying capacity** of the LVM3 is expected to increase from the current **4 tonnes** to approximately **6 tonnes** to **Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO)**.
 
 
 
• **Development Agency:**
 
 
• The **Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC)** is the lead center for the design and development of this high-thrust semi-cryogenic engine.
 
• Ongoing tests like the **EPHTA** are precursors to the **integrated engine testing** and eventual flight qualification.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Propellant Advantages:** **Isrosene** is an eco-friendly, refined version of kerosene. It is much easier to handle at **ambient temperatures** compared to **liquid hydrogen**, which must be kept at **-253 degrees Celsius**.
 
• **Future Missions:** This propulsion technology is vital for **India's future heavy-lift** missions and the **Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV)**, which aims to provide low-cost access to space.
 
• **Success Milestones:** This **3.5-second** test followed a series of **low-pressure** and **intermediate-pressure** tests, marking a significant milestone in India's journey toward self-reliance in advanced rocket propulsion.
</ul

questions.question: The joint maritime drill between the Indian Navy and the Royal Navy that began on 05 October 2025 along India’s western seaboard was known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**KONKAN-25**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The joint maritime drill known as **KONKAN-25** is a bilateral exercise conducted between the **Indian Navy** and the **Royal Navy** of the **United Kingdom**.
 
• This edition of the exercise commenced on **05 October 2025** and was hosted along **India’s western seaboard**, highlighting the growing strategic partnership between the two nations.
 
• The primary objective of **KONKAN-25** is to enhance **interoperability**, facilitate the exchange of best practices, and strengthen maritime cooperation in the **Indian Ocean Region**.
 
• The exercise involved a series of complex naval maneuvers, including **anti-surface warfare**, **anti-air warfare**, and **anti-submarine warfare** drills, aimed at maintaining a high state of readiness.
 
• Participation included **guided-missile frigates**, **destroyers**, and **maritime patrol aircraft** from both the **Indian Navy** and the **Royal Navy**, showcasing advanced naval capabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exercise KONKAN:**
 
 
• The **KONKAN** series of exercises was institutionalized in the **year 2004** and has since grown in scale and complexity.
 
• It is named after the **Konkan Coast**, which refers to the rugged section of the western coastline of **India**, spanning parts of **Maharashtra**, **Goa**, and **Karnataka**.
 
• These exercises serve as a cornerstone of **India-UK maritime relations**, ensuring stability and security in the critical sea lines of communication.
 
 
 
• **Other Indo-UK Military Exercises:**
 
 
• **Exercise Ajeya Warrior:** A biennial training event conducted between the **Indian Army** and the **British Army** to enhance counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism operations.
 
• **Exercise Indradhanush:** A joint air force exercise between the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** and the **Royal Air Force (RAF)** focusing on air combat tactics and aerial refueling.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Significance of the Western Seaboard:**
 
 
• The **Western Seaboard** of India is a vital maritime zone guarded by the **Western Naval Command**, which is headquartered in **Mumbai**.
 
• It plays a crucial role in safeguarding **India's exclusive economic zone (EEZ)** and protecting maritime trade routes against piracy and other unconventional threats.
 
 
 
• **International Maritime Cooperation:**
 
 
• Joint drills like **KONKAN-25** reflect **India's** commitment to the **"Security and Growth for All in the Region" (SAGAR)** initiative, promoting collective security and prosperity.
 
• The **Royal Navy** often deploys its **Carrier Strike Group (CSG)** or individual warships to participate in such bilateral engagements to demonstrate global reach and influence.

questions.question: ‘Expanding Quality Higher Education through States and State Public Universities’ is a report released in February 2025 by:

__
 
• The report titled **‘Expanding Quality Higher Education through States and State Public Universities’** was released in **February 2025** by **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India).
 
• The primary focus of this report is to strengthen **State Public Universities (SPUs)**, which are considered the backbone of India's higher education system, catering to the vast majority of students across the **country**.
 
• It emphasizes the **reorganization** and **revitalization** of these institutions to align with the goals set out in the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**.
 
• The report highlights that while **Centrally Funded Technical Institutes (CFTIs)** receive significant attention, **State Public Universities** account for nearly **85%** of the total student enrollment in higher education, making their improvement crucial for national development.
 
• The document provides a **roadmap** for states to enhance **academic quality**, **research output**, and **administrative efficiency** within their respective university systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• Established on **January 1, 2015**, it replaced the erstwhile **Planning Commission**. It serves as the apex public policy **think tank** of the **Government of India**.
 
• The **Prime Minister** serves as the **Ex-officio Chairperson**, while the **Vice-Chairperson** is appointed directly by the Prime Minister.
 
• It focuses on **Cooperative Federalism**, ensuring that states are active partners in the national development agenda.
 
 
 
• **State Public Universities (SPUs):**
 
 
• These are universities established or incorporated by a **State Act**. They are primarily funded by the respective **State Governments**.
 
• According to the **All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE)**, these institutions face challenges such as **faculty shortages**, **limited financial autonomy**, and **infrastructure gaps** compared to central institutions.
 
• The **February 2025** report suggests a **collaborative funding model** where the **Central Government** and **State Governments** work together to boost the **Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER)**.
 
 
 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020:**
 
 
• The policy aims to increase the **Gross Enrolment Ratio** in higher education, including vocational education, from **26.3% (2018)** to **50%** by the **year 2035**.
 
• It promotes **multidisciplinary education** and moves away from rigid silos of subjects, a theme central to the **NITI Aayog** report.
 
 
 
• **Other Educational Bodies:**
 
 
• **University Grants Commission (UGC):** A statutory body set up by the **Department of Higher Education** in **1956**, responsible for maintaining standards of university education in **India**.
 
• **Ministry of Education:** Formerly the Ministry of Human Resource Development, it is the parent ministry responsible for the implementation of **educational laws** and **national policies**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The report suggests that states should create a **State Higher Education Council (SHEC)** to better coordinate between the **state government** and **universities**.
 
• It identifies that **financial sustainability** is a major hurdle, recommending that **SPUs** explore **alumni funding**, **industry partnerships**, and **consultancy services** to diversify their **revenue streams**.
 
• The **2025** report also touches upon the **digital transformation** of higher education, advocating for better **ICT infrastructure** in rural and semi-urban **locations** to bridge the **digital divide**.

• The first ceremony was held in **2000** in **Monte Carlo**, where **Tiger Woods** and **Marion Jones** were the initial winners.

• **Rebeca Andrade**: A **Brazilian** gymnast who won **five** medals at the **2023 World Championships**, providing stiff competition to Biles.
